findings.title: The later horizon is already held in readiness
findings.claim: The focus names those who do not accept the afterlife, then says a painful punishment has already been prepared for them. In 4:18 the same prepared-painful consequence is repeated after death arrives before a plea to repent now, so the focus's later horizon is presented alongside a consequence already held ready.
findings.mechanism: The carriers are the negated trust phrase, the definite afterlife phrase, the preparation verb, and the pain adjective in 17:10. The wider 23:74 repeats the afterlife-denial condition and associates it with turning from the path; 4:18 repeats the prepared-painful wording at a death-bound appeal. These contacts bring present refusal and an already-prepared response into the same temporal relation, changing the future consequence from an indefinitely distant threat to something held in readiness.
findings.reader_payoff: The warning's later horizon remains intact, while its consequence becomes newly present as a prepared response rather than a remote possibility.
findings.containment: The locally selected referent remains the afterlife. The posteriority branch adds only its core later/other relation; it is not a claim that this branch itself lexically means the afterlife. The packet does not date the focus's punishment or equate the two passages' audiences, and target morphology is not supplied.

epistemic.reason: A trusted cross-run publication supports the focus relation and its word-to-branch mappings; a legacy-unbound reader walk is an exact semantic duplicate. The target Arabic for 4:18 and 23:74 is present, but target morphology is not, so the wider contact remains qualified.

findings.title: Preparation within an ordered account
findings.claim: The focus's preparation verb places the painful consequence in readiness for a defined group. The pericope's promise and personal-record sequence, echoed by 82:5's before-and-after accounting frame, lets that readiness read within an order of answerability rather than as an improvised reaction.
findings.mechanism: The carrier is the perfect preparation verb in 17:10. The supplied reader-walk account of 17:5 and 17:7's arriving promises and 17:13–15's written record, self-reckoning, and nontransferable burden meets that carrier as an ordered return; 82:5 adds the wider frame of what each soul has sent ahead and left behind. This contact changes preparation into readiness situated within personal accounting.
findings.reader_payoff: The prepared consequence gains an accountable shape: readiness belongs to a sequence of recorded acts and return, not an impulse introduced at judgment.
findings.containment: The 17:5, 17:7, and 17:13–15 descriptions come from legacy-unbound reader summaries, not supplied context Arabic. The target Arabic for 82:5 is present but its morphology is not; that verse does not itself name this punishment or group.

epistemic.reason: The focus branch and carrier align exactly, and the wider 82:5 target is supplied. The pericope accounting relation is reported by legacy-unbound supports without context surfaces, so its role is retained with explicit qualification.

findings.title: The denied horizon reaches present orientation
findings.claim: Across the supplied wider echoes, the focus's denial of the afterlife also has a present reach: other passages attach the same horizon-denial to preference for immediate life, deeds made attractive with bewilderment, and a concealed barrier during Quran recitation.
findings.mechanism: The carriers are the focus's afterlife phrase and negated trust verb. In 10:7, lack of expectation of meeting is paired with contentment in immediate life; 16:107 explicitly connects disbelief with preferring this life over the afterlife; 27:4 repeats the denial beside beautified deeds and wandering; and 17:45 repeats the group description in a recitation scene with a hidden barrier. The recurring denial meets these distinct present-facing consequences, so the focus's group condition reads as an orientation affecting conduct and reception as well as a belief about what follows.
findings.reader_payoff: The later horizon becomes perceptible as a present criterion: it bears on what is preferred, how deeds appear, and how recitation is received.
findings.containment: These targets are supplied at ayah level without target morphology. The finding does not claim that every person in the focus shares one motive, that the target scenes have identical audiences, or that a particular causal mechanism is established.

epistemic.reason: The focus carrier is supplied with resolved Arabic analysis and the connected target Arabic is present. Connection rows provide nominations rather than target morphology, so the cross-ayah relation is retained at ayah level.
